chapter: The craft of the ad lib player
title: Pitch and tone as the bassist's challenge
summary: He explains tuning against sections of different pitch and getting the A in a small group.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, what are the hardest things to keep under control or to conquer on the bass?

Tone, for one thing; awareness of pitch, for another, because the basses, after you're tuned up, you're already in a fixed position. So in big orchestras they have string sections, reed sections, brass sections. Each section is different. The string section is generally sharp because each violinist wants to be heard a little more

than the other ones, so he tunes up a little sharper.
By the time it comes to the bass, if you keep
attuned to them, you have to turn your string up a little bit.
And then that passage ends, and you go to the trumpets, and
they're flat.

You got to turn down again. And then the reeds in between,
you know, so it just -- it's a challenge. It's a nice
challenge. It keeps you where you should be, alerted.
What about in a small group?
A small group isn't too bad.

Uh-huh. You're attuned to the piano
at the start?

Well, I get the A from the piano, but,
you see, a piano can vary with all the different octaves.
I have to get the bass A, but I have to get the A in order to
know where I am. Then whatever else happens, then I can
follow that.
